definition: Ethanol is produced from starch-based crops using fermentation, the same basic process used to make alcoholic beverages.
core_idea: Raw crop material is milled into meal, mixed with liquid and heated to dissolve it and kill bacteria, cooled and treated with enzymes to convert starch into sugar, then fermented with yeast into alcohol and carbon dioxide, and finally distilled to separate the alcohol.
key_points: Raw materials are milled into a fine powder called meal
Liquid is added to the meal to form a slurry, which is heated to dissolve the meal and kill bacteria
The mixture is cooled and enzymes are added to convert starch into simpler sugars
Yeast is added to convert the sugars into alcohol and carbon dioxide
The alcohol is separated from remaining solids/liquids by distillation
